title: Environment variables, packages and background jobs

questions.q: Why should Bazaar's database password come from an environment variable instead of the code?
options: The code (and Git) never contains the secret, and the same code can run with different settings on each server
Python can't read passwords from code
questions.explain: Code ends up in Git and is shared. Settings and secrets belong outside it.

questions.q: You type DB_PASSWORD=secret123, then python3 settings.py says DB_PASSWORD is not set. Why?
options: It's only a shell variable; programs get it only after export
questions.explain: export DB_PASSWORD puts it in the environment, which every program started from that shell receives.

questions.q: What does DB_PASSWORD=secret123 python3 settings.py do?
options: Gives the setting to that one command only; the shell doesn't keep it
Exports it for every future command
questions.explain: A setting written in front of a command, on the same line, applies to that command alone.

questions.q: apt-get install -y jq says "E: Unable to locate package jq". What should you do first?
options: apt-get update, to download the latest package list
questions.explain: apt needs a fresh list of what's available. In Docker images the list is usually removed to save space.

questions.q: What does the & do in python3 import_products.py > import.log 2>&1 &?
options: Runs it in the background, so you get your prompt back immediately
Joins it with the next command
questions.explain: jobs lists background jobs, kill %1 stops job 1, and wait waits for them to finish.

questions.q: In Python, os.environ.get("DEBUG") returns "false". Why is if os.environ.get("DEBUG"): a bug?
options: Environment values are text, and the text "false" is not empty, so it counts as true

questions.q: (Going deeper) A script runs export SALE=diwali. After it ends, your terminal still has no SALE. Why?
options: The script ran in a child process with its own copy of the environment; changes don't flow back to the shell
questions.explain: To change the current shell from a file, source it: source script.sh.

questions.q: (Going deeper) A job must keep running after you log out. What's the quick way, and the proper way?
options: nohup command > job.log 2>&1 & for a quick fix; a systemd service for anything long-lived
questions.explain: nohup ignores the hang-up signal sent at logout. Services (Lesson 7) also restart the job after crashes and reboots.
